parsed.headline: Advance voter turnout increases for Toronto's 2026 municipal election

pages.text: A total of 222,550 eligible voters participated during six days of advance voting for Toronto's 2026 municipal election, which concluded on October 11, 2026, at 7 p.m. According to CBC Toronto, this represents the largest turnout in over a decade and a nearly 72 per cent increase compared to the 129,000 early votes recorded during the 2023 mayoral byelection. Election day is scheduled for October 26, 2026, at which time voters must go to their assigned voting places as indicated on their Voter Information Card or the Toronto Elections website. For those using mail-in ballots, the City of Toronto stated that completed packages must be returned to Toronto Elections by noon on October 14, 2026. To meet this deadline, voters are advised to use one of 25 secure, indoor yellow drop boxes located in each ward across the city. These boxes are monitored by CCTV and emptied daily by staff. Additionally, registration for third party advertisers, which includes any person, corporation, or trade union intending to spend money to promote, support, or oppose a candidate, closed at 4:30 p.m. on October 9, 2026.

A recent survey from Liaison Strategies conducted during the advance voting period suggests incumbent Mayor Olivia Chow leads the mayoral race by five points, polling at 51 per cent among decided and leaning voters. Councillor Brad Bradford is polling at 46 per cent. In response to the survey and the high advance turnout, Chow’s team credited the results to the efforts of volunteers campaigning across the city. Conversely, Laryssa Waler, a spokesperson for Bradford’s campaign, stated that the high early turnout indicates voters want a change in leadership.

parsed.headline: Suspected cholera cases triple in Yemen over three weeks, WHO reports

pages.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned that suspected cholera cases in Yemen have tripled within a three-week period. According to a WHO report released on Tuesday, suspected cases rose from 217 during the week of September 6–12 to 647 during the week of September 27 to October 3. This surge comes as renewed fighting has displaced more than 200,000 people, driving civilians into unsanitary camps. Annette Heinzelmann, the WHO emergency director for the region, stated that families fleeing conflict are facing threats from preventable and treatable diseases, noting that outbreaks could spread rapidly without urgent funding and access to safe water, vaccination, and essential health services. This year, Yemen has reported 8,034 suspected cases and 27 deaths, with one-quarter of those cases occurring in the last four weeks. The disease has also reached remote displacement camps in Hadramout in the east, which are noted as being particularly difficult for medical teams to access. In the southwest, five governorates hosting large numbers of displaced people—Abyan, Lahij, al-Dhalea, Taiz, and Aden—account for 92 percent of reported cases. The WHO noted that the surge exacerbates stress on hospitals already burdened by war casualties. Cholera has fluctuated in Yemen for years during the ongoing conflict between the Houthis, an armed group known as Ansar Allah, and the internationally recognized Yemeni government. In 2017, a wave of the disease infected hundreds of thousands and killed at least 2,000 people.

parsed.headline: Majority on Ghana's Foreign Affairs Committee rejects Minority claims over GH¢49.7m South Africa evacuation expenditure

pages.text: The Majority on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee in Ghana has rejected allegations from the Minority that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs failed to account for GH¢49.7 million spent on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa. The caucus described the Minority's claims as “dubious political mischief.” Dr. Alfred Okoe Vanderpuije, the Chairman of the Committee, dismissed the allegations and insisted the Ministry had accounted for the expenditure. Dr. Vanderpuije stated that a document exceeding 200 pages, submitted in response to a request under the Right to Information (RTI) law, provides details of the costs incurred during the evacuation exercise. He maintained that the records presented by the Ministry contradict the Minority’s claims of non-accountability. While the Minority insists the Ministry must provide a full account of the funds, the Majority maintains that the submitted documents adequately address the concerns. Consequently, the Majority is calling on the Attorney-General to initiate a forensic investigation into all evacuation exercises undertaken by the former New Patriotic Party (NPP) government.

parsed.headline: Ghanaian Finance Minister leads delegation to IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok

pages.text: Ghanaian Minister of Finance, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, is leading a delegation to the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group in Bangkok, Thailand. Scheduled for October 12–18, 2026, the meetings involve finance ministers, central bank governors—including the Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama—and other senior global officials to address pressing global economic challenges. According to Graphic Online, this gathering is the first held outside Washington, D.C., since Dr Forson assumed office in 2025. The meetings occur as Ghana prepares to transition from economic stabilisation toward sustained transformation following the conclusion of its $3 billion bailout programme. Dr Forson is expected to engage in bilateral and multilateral discussions with IMF leadership, senior World Bank officials, and other international financial institutions and development partners to reassure investors regarding Ghana's economic outlook and commitment to reforms.

The meetings in Bangkok follow a period where Bretton Woods institutions provided positive assessments of Ghana's progress in restoring economic stability after the 2022 crisis. Dr Forson is expected to unveil the government's New Economy programme, described as a blueprint for the country's next phase of economic development, during the presentation of the 2027 Budget and Economic Statement to Parliament in November. Africanews reports that the broader IMF and World Bank meetings, which include activities starting October 10, 2026, take place amid global economic pressures such as energy shocks, rising debt, and the impact of artificial intelligence. IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva noted that the global economy is facing a negative energy supply shock and a positive demand shock from AI, with impacts being highly uneven globally.

parsed.headline: MI5 chief says Russia attempted to interfere in Brexit referendum with little impact

pages.text: Ken McCallum, the head of Britain’s domestic intelligence agency MI5, stated on Tuesday that Moscow attempted to interfere in the 2016 Brexit referendum through social media and television reports, but noted a significant difference between what was attempted and what actually resulted. McCallum said the interference had little impact and that neither tactic was particularly sophisticated or successful. During an annual threat update, the spy chief reported that Russian-owned English-language broadcasters RT and Sputnik provided biased anti-migration and anti-EU coverage around the time of the referendum. He also identified a second line of attempted interference involving an unspecified number of internet trolls using fake social media accounts, operating largely on X, to influence the result.

Previous studies have cited these interference attempts. The digital campaign group 89up reported that RT and Sputnik published 261 mostly misleading articles regarding immigration and anti-EU issues, which achieved 134 million potential page impressions. Other studies have reported on a state-linked Russian ``troll army'' tweeting about the referendum, though estimates of the number of active accounts have varied between 54 and 150,000. McCallum endorsed comments made by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who raised the issue of Russian interference over the past two days, though McCallum cautioned that continuing the debate risked providing the Kremlin with a needless propaganda victory.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh Education Minister calls for teacher proficiency in technology and AI

pages.text: Bangladesh Education Minister Dr. A N M Ehsanul Hoque Milon stated on Tuesday that teachers must acquire comprehensive knowledge of technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to effectively educate students in a technology-driven world. Speaking at the inauguration of an orientation training course for 49th BCS (General Education) cadre officers at the Rural Development Academy (RDA) in Bogura, Milon noted that students are currently highly proficient in information technology, necessitating that teachers update their own technological skills and knowledge. The minister also emphasized the importance of research for improving the education system and developing the teaching community. During the event, Milon urged teachers to perform their duties with sincerity and dedication, rising above political differences to assist in building a modern Bangladesh.

The eight-day orientation programme is being attended by 613 newly recruited BCS General Education cadre officers. The event was presided over by Dr. Sardar Md Keramat Ali, Secretary (routine charge) of the Secondary and Higher Education Division, with a welcome address delivered by Prof. Dr. Wasim Md Mezbahaul Haque, Director General of the National Academy for Educational Management (NAEM). Special guests included BNP Executive Committee member Rezaul Karim Badsha, MP; Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal Vice-President Nazmun Nahar Baby; Director General of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education Prof. Dr. Khan Moinuddin Al Mahmud Sohel; and Acting Director General of RDA Bogura Md Abdul Majid Pramanik. Additionally, Milon informed journalists that the government is planning to arrange supplementary examinations within 15 days of publishing Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination results for students who fail in up to two subjects, an initiative intended to prevent students from losing an entire academic year.

parsed.headline: Toronto cyclists seek Supreme Court of Canada appeal over provincial bike lane removal plan

pages.text: Cyclists challenging a plan by the Ontario government to remove major bike lanes in Toronto are seeking leave to appeal to the Supreme Court of Canada. On October 13, 2026, the cycling advocacy charity Cycle Toronto announced it would pursue the appeal, the same day Ontario stated it would begin removing bike lanes along parts of Bloor Street W. in Etobicoke. The legal challenge concerns a provincial plan to replace 19 kilometres of bike lanes with car lanes across three major roads. While a lower court initially ruled the plan was an unconstitutional risk to cyclist safety, the Ontario Court of Appeal overturned that decision in an August ruling, stating the trial judge had improperly engaged in policy-making and political considerations. Cycle Toronto and its co-applicants are being represented by the environmental law charity Ecojustice and the firm Paliare Roland Rosenberg Rothstein LLP. At a Tuesday morning news conference, Michael Longfield, executive director of Cycle Toronto, stated that bike lanes do not cause traffic congestion and alleged that removing them would put lives at risk. Bronwyn Roe, a staff lawyer with Ecojustice, said the group is asking the Supreme Court to hear the case to provide clarity regarding the scope of rights to life and security of the person protected by Section 7 of the Charter.

parsed.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine received no early warning of Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv

pages.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine received no early warning from partners regarding a Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv on October 12, 2026. Zelenskyy described the attack, in which five missiles hit civilian infrastructure, as “particularly vile” and noted that receiving intelligence from western allies is critical for preventing deaths. While he did not apportion blame for the lack of warning, he stated that Russia “did not heed” the call for a ceasefire made by US President Donald Trump. 13 October 2026 reporting indicates that while US officials had threatened to halt intelligence sharing with Kyiv over the weekend, Trump denied that sharing had stopped, telling reporters that the US is sharing intelligence and working with both Ukraine and Russia to end the war. Trump has previously demanded that Ukraine cease attacks on Russian oil refineries and has blamed Zelenskyy for rising fuel prices in the US. Despite speculations regarding intelligence ties, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha insisted that intelligence cooperation with the US has continued.
